title: Church of the Eternal Flame
content:
## The Church of the Eternal Flame

The dominant religious institution of Veltria, claiming the spiritual adherence of approximately **72% of the population**. Founded in the twelfth century around the doctrine of the Eternal Flame — a symbol of divine constancy in a world of change — the Church has been the social backbone of Veltrian life for eight centuries.

## Theology and Structure

The Church teaches a monotheism focused on the Flame as the eternal presence of the divine in the material world. Its hierarchy is structured: the **Archbishop** (currently Stanislov Renek) at the apex, a College of Bishops, parish priests at the community level. The Archbishop's political influence is informal but substantial — a public statement from the Cathedral can shift rural opinion faster than any newspaper.

## The Halvek Question

The Church's record during the Halvek regime is the central unresolved question in its current political position. Archbishop Benedikt Goral — Renek's predecessor — publicly blessed Halvek's assumption of power in 1934 and called the 1897 constitution "the work of godless agitators." Church properties were never subjected to BNI surveillance. Church schools received state funding throughout the regime.

The current Archbishop, **Stanislov Renek**, describes this period as "a time in which the Church, like all institutions, made difficult choices in difficult circumstances." His critics describe it differently.

## Political Role in 1963

The Church retains extraordinary influence in rural Veltria, particularly Thornfeld. Its hospitals, schools, and charitable organizations are often the only social services available in small communities. It is simultaneously a genuine moral force, a powerful political actor, and an institution that has not been held to account for its complicity in twenty-six years of authoritarian rule.

Archbishop Renek is not Goral. He is more careful, more politically sophisticated, and genuinely uncertain about the new government. He has not moved against it. He has not endorsed it. He is waiting.

title: The Halvekists
content:
## The Halvekists

The Halvekists are the political heirs of **General Edvard Halvek** and the Veltrian Unity Front that governed the Republic from 1934 until Halvek's death in 1960. They form the largest opposition bloc in the National Parliament, holding roughly one-third of the seats, and they speak for a substantial part of the older generation who remember the Halvek years as a time of order, steel, and new roads.

Their politics are authoritarian nationalism. They defend the Halvek Constitution as a sound instrument that weak successors misused, they favour a state-directed economy, and they regard the Bureau of National Integrity as a necessary guardian of the nation rather than an instrument of terror. Their parliamentary leader, **Dražen Kolvar**, has used committees, amendments, and procedural delay to slow nearly every reform bill the government has introduced.

Halvekist sympathies are strongest among older voters, parts of the officer corps, and communities that prospered under the old regime's infrastructure programmes. The Dravenni question remains the sharpest point of division between them and the reform movement.

- **Leader:** Dražen Kolvar, Leader of the Opposition
- **Parliamentary strength:** roughly one-third of the seats
- **Core demands:** Retain the Halvek Constitution, restore full BNI powers, reject minority-language concessions
- **Relationship to the government:** Open opposition, with a standing threat to block or delay every reform in the Assembly

title: The Workers' Coalition
content:
## The Workers' Coalition

The Workers' Unity Coalition is the Republic's organised labour left. Its base is the industrial heartland of **Kravenstal**, where its meeting hall occupies a converted textile factory and its walls are lined with photographs of past strikes. It is led by **Soraya Khaled**, a former political prisoner who spent eight years in a Halvek prison and who trusts few politicians, including the Chancellor.

The Coalition describes itself as democratic socialist. It wants key industries brought into public or worker ownership, universal healthcare and education, workers' councils with real authority in the factories, and a tax burden shifted onto the country's wealthiest families. Its members have a long memory of wage cuts, unsafe mines, and unpaid work, and they judge every government by how it treats the people who run the machines.

The Coalition can shut down the economy through general strikes, and it has the discipline to do so. It can also become the government's most committed ally if its demands are taken seriously. If the government is seen to draw too close to the Orythian Dominion, the Coalition's alignment will attract hostile attention from the Arcturian Commonwealth.

- **Leader:** Soraya Khaled
- **Strength:** Mass support among Kravenstal's workers and in the labour movement
- **Core demands:** Nationalisation of key industry, workers' councils, universal public services, taxation of the wealthy
- **Relationship to the government:** Conditional partner, quick to mobilise if labour concerns are ignored

title: The Reformist Bloc
content:
## The Reformist Bloc

The Reformist Bloc is the Civic Renewal coalition that carried the February 1963 election and that **Katerin Ashavel** leads as Chancellor. It is the government's own base: an alliance of liberal democrats, constitutional lawyers, journalists, university academics, and reform-minded professionals who want the Republic to become a free and accountable state.

Its programme is liberal democracy. It seeks a new constitution that strips power from the Chancellorship, an independent judiciary, free and fair elections, the dissolution of the Bureau of National Integrity, and enforceable minority rights. Its intellectual leader is **Professor Aldric Theron**, whose draft constitution the Bloc intends to defend.

The Bloc's strength lies in **Ashenmere**, where its support is deepest, and in the universities and independent press that give it a public voice. Its weakness is that its members are idealists in a pragmatic world. They are impatient with compromise and quick to accuse the government of betrayal when reform is slowed. The military and the old establishment have watched the Bloc closely, and the Bloc knows that moving too fast invites a backlash.

- **Leader:** The Chancellor, with Professor Aldric Theron as principal intellectual figure
- **Strength:** Ashenmere, the universities, and the independent press
- **Core demands:** A new constitution, judicial independence, BNI dissolution, minority rights
- **Relationship to the government:** The governing base itself, and its most demanding critic

title: The Iron Covenant
content:
## The Iron Covenant

The Iron Covenant is the military-nationalist right. It is led by **General Oskar Brenner**, Army Chief of Staff and a protégé of Edvard Halvek. Its influence is concentrated in the officer corps and among nationalist voters in the border province of **Sevagrad**, which has lived under the shadow of the Tyvaren Confederation for decades.

Its doctrine is militaristic nationalism. It calls for a large defence budget, closed borders, a firm stance against Tyvaren, and the removal of what it calls "foreign elements" from public life. It treats refugees from Morivask as a security threat and regards the Dravenni as a question of loyalty. It speaks of national security in the language of necessity, and its supporters often describe their position as patriotism rather than extremism.

The Iron Covenant votes as a bloc in the Assembly and is more disciplined than its rivals. Its real power is not its vote count but its access to the armed forces. Brenner allowed the democratic transition to proceed because he believed he could manage the new government. If the Covenant comes to believe that its position is being destroyed, elements of the officer corps may act without waiting for parliament.

- **Leader:** General Oskar Brenner, Army Chief of Staff
- **Strength:** The officer corps and nationalist opinion in Sevagrad
- **Core demands:** Larger defence spending, closed borders, a hard line on Tyvaren, purge of "foreign elements"
- **Relationship to the government:** Hostile and dangerous; the Chancellor must manage the military without surrendering to it

title: The Business Consortium
content:
## The Business Consortium

The Business Consortium speaks for the Republic's commercial and financial interests, from banks and industrial concerns to the shipping and trading houses of **Aldenmoor**. Its most powerful individual voice is **Margrave Lucan Vael**, whose steel and mining holdings give him influence well beyond his own enterprises, and whose fortune was built under the old regime's contracts.

Its doctrine is market liberalism. It favours private investment, low taxation of enterprise, lighter regulation, the sale of state industries, and open trade with the Arcturian Commonwealth. It argues that Veltria's recovery depends on confidence, and it measures the government by whether capital stays in the country.

The Consortium's greatest weapon is the threat of capital flight. Investment can be moved offshore quietly, and a loss of business confidence can damage the economy faster than any strike. Its critics argue that its members will trade public welfare for private advantage, and they point to the mine safety scandal as an example of business interests resisting accountability.

- **Key figure:** Margrave Lucan Vael, a leading steel and mining magnate
- **Strength:** Finance in Ashenmere, shipping in Aldenmoor, and the major industrial concerns
- **Core demands:** Private investment, deregulation, privatisation of state industry, low taxation
- **Relationship to the government:** Conditional; cooperative if investment is protected, openly hostile if it is threatened

title: The Dravenni
content:
## The Dravenni

The Dravenni are the Republic's principal ethnic minority, roughly eight percent of the population, concentrated in the mountainous north of **Dravenhollow**. Their language was banned from public use under the Halvek regime, their traditional representative body, the Council of Elders, was dissolved by central decree, and forty thousand Dravenni were forcibly displaced from their ancestral lands during the Silent Clearances.

The Dravenni political movement is divided. The Dravenni Council seeks recognition of the language, a measure of autonomy for Dravenhollow, and the restoration of its standing. The **Dravenni Liberation Front** is an underground organisation led by **Idris Kaelen**, who was wanted by the old regime. Its demands are more radical: full acknowledgement of the Clearances, land restitution, and in some factions full secession. The Front has also been reported in contact with Tyvaren intelligence, which offers money and weapons to some Dravenni, so the government must distinguish between the two wings.

The Dravenni question is a test of the Republic's commitment to human rights. Recognition of their language would win international goodwill and reassure Dravenni communities across the eastern border in Morivask, but it would enrage nationalists and the Church.

- **Leaders:** The Dravenni Council; Idris Kaelen of the Liberation Front
- **Strength:** Dravenhollow's population and the sympathy of minority communities across the region
- **Core demands:** Official language recognition, Dravenhollow autonomy, acknowledgement of the Clearances, land restitution
- **Relationship to the government:** Unresolved; a peaceful settlement is possible, but refusal risks an armed insurgency
